source: NCERT Class VIII, Resources and Development, Geography Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. What is a Resource
points: A **resource** = anything that has **utility (use/value)** and can satisfy human needs.
Something becomes a resource only when its **utility is realised** and technology allows its use.
The value depends on **utility, technology, and human need**.

sub: **Biotic** — from the living world (plants, animals, humans).
**Abiotic** — from the non-living world (rocks, minerals, water, land).
**Renewable** — can be renewed/reproduced (solar, wind, water, forests).
**Non-renewable** — limited, take very long to form (coal, petroleum, minerals).
**Actual** — quantity known and being used now.
**Potential** — exists but not yet used (e.g. undiscovered/unutilised).

points.text: **By ownership/distribution:** individual, community, national, international; **ubiquitous** (found everywhere, e.g. air) vs **localised** (found in some places, e.g. minerals).

sections.heading: 3. Conservation and Sustainable Development
points: Resources are limited and unevenly distributed; **over-use** leads to problems.
**Conservation** = using resources **carefully and giving them time to renew**.
**Sustainable development** = development that meets **present needs without harming the ability of future generations** to meet their needs.
**Agenda 21** (Rio Earth Summit, 1992) is a global action plan for sustainable development.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Resource = anything with utility satisfying human needs (needs utility + technology + need).
By development: actual (in use) vs potential (not yet used); ubiquitous vs localised.
Sustainable development = meet present needs without harming future generations; Agenda 21 (Rio 1992).

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Actual** resources are being used now; **potential** resources exist but are not yet used.
**Ubiquitous** = found everywhere (air); **localised** = found only in some places (copper ore).
**Sustainable development** balances **present and future** needs; framework = **Agenda 21 (1992)**.
